title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant - Full-Time or Part-Time

Flexible Working Hours Hybrid Working (3 days office/2 WFH) Study Support Available

We are working with a well-established and growing business to recruit and Accounts Assistant. This is a great opportunity for someone looking for a role where the working environment, flexibility and finding the right fit is just as important as experience.
- Competitive salary + additional employee benefits including Study Support if required.
- You will be joining a small, approachable finance team, providing support with the day-to-day financial operations of the business.
- The organisation is investing in technology, automation and new systems, so this would suit someone who is comfortable using technology, open to new ways of working and interested in how finance is evolving.

The Job:

Working in a friendly, easy going and supportive team, duties will include but not limited to:
- Maintaining the Purchase Ledger.
- Updating and maintaining the cashbook.
- Assisting with credit card reconciliations and expenses.
- Bank reconciliations.
- Other ad hoc duties as required.

The person:
- Experience within a similar environment is required.
- A positive, "can-do" attitude is essential.
- Good IT skills are essential.

title: Credit Controller
company: Chase and Holland Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Credit Controller - Brigg - Up to £35,000

Are you an experienced Credit Controller looking for a role where you can really make an impact, take ownership and be part of an ambitious, market-leading business?

Chase & Holland are delighted to be supporting a well-established, market-leading business in North Lincolnshire as they look to strengthen their finance team with the appointment of an experienced Credit Controller.

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a large, ambitious organisation where your contribution will play a key role in protecting cash flow, managing financial risk and building lasting customer relationships. Offering far more than simply chasing overdue payments, this is a varied and rewarding position where you'll work closely with customers, sales teams and wider business stakeholders to drive results.

What's in it for you?
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Subsidised meals at two on-site restaurants
- Access to an on-site gym
- Excellent health and wellbeing support, including free annual eye tests, contributions towards glasses and mental health first aid support
- Regular team and company social events and fundraising days
- Up to 50% discount on company products after one year's service
- Free on-site parking

Credit Controller Responsibilities:
- Proactively managing overdue debt and maximising cash collection across customer accounts.
- Building and maintaining strong relationships with customers and sales managers to effectively manage and mitigate credit risk.
- Reviewing customer credit limits and ensuring balances remain within agreed terms.
- Accurately allocating customer payments and maintaining customer account information.
- Preparing payment applications, sales invoices and customer statements, ensuring all supporting documentation is provided.
- Working closely with internal stakeholders to manage product dispatch approvals and associated invoicing.
- Taking ownership of customer queries, investigating discrepancies and driving timely resolutions.
- Completing final account reconciliations and managing retentions.
- Maintaining financial integrity, protecting business assets and ensuring transactional service level agreements are achieved.

What we're looking for:
- Proven experience within a Credit Control or similar position.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
- Strong analytical skills and exceptional attention to detail.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills, with the ability to effectively prioritise workloads.
- A proactive, results-driven individual who enjoys taking ownership, solving problems and working both independently and collaboratively.

Why Apply?
If you're passionate about credit control and enjoy a role that combines relationship building, problem-solving and delivering tangible results, this could be the perfect next step.

If you're interested in finding out more about this exciting Credit Controller opportunity, please click 'Apply Now'.
Chase & Holland acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. We specialise in finance, supply chain, HR, IT and office support recruitment and comfortably service Yorkshire, Derbyshire, Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire, Staffordshire and Lincolnshire.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller Gainsborough 12 Month FTC

Reed finance are partnering with a well established, market leading organisation who are looking to add a credit controller to their finance team on a 12 month contract to support with increased workload.

In this role you will play a key role in managing accounts in the UK and Europe, ensuring cash collection targets are achieved while maintaining customer relationships.

Key responsibilities include:
- Managing outstanding debt and ensuring prompt payment of invoices.
- Chasing overdue accounts via telephone, email, and written correspondence.
- Monitoring customer credit limits and supporting credit risk management processes.
- Processing new account applications, conducting credit checks, and setting up customer accounts.
- Reviewing orders on credit hold and making timely credit decisions.
- Posting cash, reconciling customer accounts, processing ledger adjustments, and resolving invoice queries.
- Working closely with European finance colleagues to support group credit control activities.
- Liaising with external collection agencies when required.
- Providing general administration support within the finance function.

About you:

This role would suit a candidate with experience in credit control or accounts receivable who has:
- Knowledge of sales ledger and accounting processes.
- Understanding of Direct Debit and SEPA payment processes.
- Strong communication and negotiation skills with a confident and professional telephone manner.
- Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively.
- A proactive, organised, and self-motivated approach

If you are an experienced accounting professional who is looking for your next challenge, this opportunity offers the chance to make an impact whilst gaining exposure to both UK and European operations.

title: Finance Administrator
description:
Finance Administrator

Grantham, Part Time (16-30 hours), Permanent

£26,000 - £29,000 per annum FTE (pro-rata, dependent on experience)

Future Prospects Group are delighted to be working with our client, an internationally renowned company based in Grantham, who are seeking an organised and dependable Finance Administrator to join their established team on a permanent, part-time basis.

This is an great opportunity to support with the day-to-day transactional finance operations within a supportive and reputable organisation. Offering rare flexibility around your working hours, including the option of a nine-day fortnight, this role is tailored for an experienced finance or accounts professional looking for meaningful work alongside an enviable work-life balance.

THE ROLE

Your responsibilities as a Finance Administrator will include:
- Maintaining company cashbooks and completing comprehensive monthly bank reconciliations.
- Posting incoming customer receipts and outgoing supplier payments accurately and in a timely manner.
- Processing and posting up to 400 purchase invoices each month, identifying and resolving any associated invoice queries.
- Carrying out regular purchase ledger and sales ledger reconciliations alongside ad-hoc credit control tasks.
- Preparing and executing the weekly supplier payment run in accordance with company schedules.
- Processing and reconciling monthly corporate credit card statements.
- Accurately posting HMRC deferred duty and VAT entries.
- Logging project labour hours on a monthly basis to support operational project tracking.
- Supporting the Finance Manager with monthly closing, year-end accounts, and annual audit preparation.

THE CANDIDATE

The ideal Finance Administrator will be able to demonstrate the following key skills and experience:
- Previous demonstrable experience working within an accounts office or finance administration capacity.
- Strong numerical capabilities paired with high attention to detail and accuracy.
- Confidence using computer systems and Microsoft Office packages, particularly Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills when liaising with colleagues, suppliers, and clients.
- A proactive mindset with a genuine enthusiasm for learning new processes and financial systems.
- The ability to work effectively under pressure and manage tasks towards tight deadlines.
- Proven capability in establishing and nurturing positive working relationships across all levels of the business.

THE BENEFITS

The benefits included with this Finance Administrator role are:
- Exceptional working flexibility offering between 16 and 30 hours per week to suit your lifestyle.
- Access to a nine-day fortnight scheme, providing every other Friday off.
- Generous annual leave entitlement of 32 days including Bank Holidays.
- Enhanced pension scheme contributions and enhanced sick pay following probation.
- Enhanced maternity and paternity pay alongside a four-times salary death in service benefit.
- Free on-site car parking, complimentary tea and coffee, eye test vouchers, and a cycle to work scheme.
- Regular company social events including a Christmas party and summer barbecue.

Thank you for your interest in this vacancy and good luck with your application.

If you have not heard from a member of the Future Prospects team within 7 days from your application, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion. Unfortunately, due to the high volume of applications we receive, we are unable to provide individual feedback.

The services of Future Prospects are those of an Employment Agency.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
We are actively recruiting for a Payroll Administrator job opportunity with an accountancy firm based close to Lincoln. The salary is negotiable and will of course depend on experience and qualification level and is open within reason. The office is commutable from locations such as Horncastle, Gainsborough, Louth, Market Rasen, and Woodhall Spa.

Responsibilities (may include all / any of the following):
- Taking responsibility for the day-to-day running of the firm's payroll division.
- Processing payrolls for a portfolio of approximately 150 clients.
- Managing workplace pension administration and submissions.
- Processing CIS returns and handling related queries.
- Ensuring all payrolls are processed accurately and within the relevant deadlines.
- Dealing with client queries and providing support and guidance on payroll-related matters.
- Ensuring compliance with relevant payroll legislation and HMRC requirements.
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring all statutory submissions are completed on time.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary in line with market rate
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays
- Pension Scheme - with employer contribution Employee assistance programme
- Hybrid working
- Free parking
- Sick pay
- Excellent office culture
- Commission scheme for client referral/introducing new clients and staff
- Flexible on part-time or full-time
- Flexible working - different start, and finish times
